summary: Configured node1 to log sudo commands exclusively to /var/log/sudo-commands.log with the invoking user and four-digit timestamp. Verified the configuration and logging behavior before and after reboot.
actions_performed: Created /etc/sudoers.d/90-command-logging with logfile, log_year, and !syslog settings.
Created the dedicated root-owned, mode-0600 log file and validated sudoers syntax.
Confirmed test commands were recorded in the dedicated log but absent from syslog, auth.log, and the journal.
Safely rebooted node1 and verified configuration, historical log data, and new command logging persisted.

evidence.requirement: Record sudo commands with user and timestamp in /var/log/sudo-commands.log
evidence.summary: Sudoers validation succeeded, and log entries show year, time, invoking user, target user, and executed command.

evidence.requirement: Keep sudo command entries out of general system logging
evidence.summary: Unique pre- and post-restart markers had zero matches in syslog/auth.log and the system journal.

Captured healthy baseline boot ID 8d1d94e2-39c3-492e-b9eb-974d111d2137, received restart acknowledgement, observed changed boot ID dc745e4d-2077-49f8-861c-1d6ddd5f469c, and verified running state, active rsyslog, valid persistent configuration, retained pre-restart data, and successful fresh logging.
